questions.question: In 2026, a scrap yard is the final processor for household refrigerators charged with R-134a, a non-exempt substitute refrigerant. Does the safe disposal section, 40 CFR 82.155, apply to them?

options.A: No, because the section applies only to appliances containing class I and class II refrigerants
options.B: Only if each refrigerator holds more than five pounds of refrigerant
options.C: Yes, because starting on January 1, 2018, it applies to appliances containing any class I or class II refrigerant or any non-exempt substitute refrigerant
options.D: Only if the refrigerators were manufactured before 2018

questions.explanation: "Starting on January 1, 2018, this section applies to disposal of appliances containing any class I or class II refrigerant or any non-exempt substitute refrigerant." The class I and class II limit applied only until that date.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.155, Safe disposal of appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Starting on January 1, 2018, this section applies to disposal of appliances containing any class I or class II refrigerant or any non-exempt substitute refrigerant.

questions.question: An office break room has an under-the-counter ice maker that was factory-sealed with 2 pounds of refrigerant. How do the definitions classify it?

options.A: As a small appliance
options.B: As industrial process refrigeration
options.C: As an MVAC-like appliance
options.D: As comfort cooling

questions.explanation: The small appliance definition names "under-the-counter ice makers" among its examples, for appliances factory-sealed "with five (5) pounds or less of refrigerant."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: room air conditioners (including window air conditioners, portable air conditioners, and packaged terminal air heat pumps), dehumidifiers, under-the-counter ice makers, vending machines, and drinking water coolers

questions.question: The technician definition also covers persons who, in the course of disposal of an appliance, could be reasonably expected to violate the integrity of the refrigerant circuit. Which appliances does that disposal part of the definition leave out?

options.A: Low-pressure appliances
options.B: Appliances with a full charge of 50 pounds or more
options.C: High-pressure and very high-pressure appliances
options.D: Small appliances, MVACs, and MVAC-like appliances

questions.explanation: Technician also means any person who in the course of disposal of an appliance "(except small appliances, MVACs, and MVAC-like appliances) could be reasonably expected to violate the integrity of the refrigerant circuit." Anyone recovering refrigerant from a small appliance for disposal still has to meet the recovery levels in 82.156(b).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Technician also means any person who in the course of disposal of an appliance (except small appliances, MVACs, and MVAC-like appliances) could be reasonably expected to violate the integrity of the refrigerant circuit and therefore release refrigerants from the appliances into the environment.

questions.question: A Type I technician's wallet-sized card must name the certifying program. Which date must the card include with the program's name?

options.A: The date the technician's certificate expires
options.B: The date the certifying program received EPA approval
options.C: The date the technician first registered as an apprentice
options.D: The date of the technician's next recertification

questions.explanation: Each card must include "the name of the certifying program including the date the certifying program received EPA approval," along with the person's name, the type of certification and a unique number.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each wallet-sized identification card must include, at a minimum, the name of the certifying program including the date the certifying program received EPA approval

questions.question: An appliance uses a substitute refrigerant in an end-use that 40 CFR 82.154(a)(1) does not list as exempt. How do the definitions classify that substitute in that end-use?

options.A: As an exempt substitute, provided the appliance holds five pounds or less
options.B: As a class II refrigerant
options.C: As a non-exempt substitute
options.D: As an exempt substitute, provided it is a hydrocarbon

questions.explanation: Exempt substitutes are certain substitutes in end-uses "specified in § 82.154(a)(1) as exempt from the venting prohibition and the requirements of this subpart," and the term non-exempt substitutes "refers to all other substitutes and end-uses not so specified in § 82.154(a)(1)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: the term “non-exempt substitutes” refers to all other substitutes and end-uses not so specified in § 82.154(a)(1).

questions.question: Every Type I test includes Group I questions. Which list matches the Group I subject areas in Appendix D?

options.A: Leak detection; recovery techniques; safety
options.B: Environmental impact of CFCs, HCFCs, and substitute refrigerants; laws and regulations; changing industry outlook
options.C: Shipping; disposal; recovery techniques
options.D: Brazing; electrical controls; system charging

questions.explanation: Group I covers "Environmental impact of CFCs, HCFCs, and substitute refrigerants," "Laws and regulations" and "Changing industry outlook." Leak detection, recovery techniques, safety, shipping and disposal are Group II areas.

questions.question: A recovery device needs the small appliance's own compressor to help remove the refrigerant. Which defined term describes this device?

options.A: Self-contained recovery equipment
options.B: Low-loss fitting
options.C: System receiver
options.D: System-dependent recovery equipment

questions.explanation: System-dependent recovery equipment is equipment "that requires the assistance of components contained in an appliance to remove the refrigerant from the appliance." Self-contained equipment works "without the assistance of components contained in the appliance."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: System-dependent recovery equipment means refrigerant recovery equipment that requires the assistance of components contained in an appliance to remove the refrigerant from the appliance.

questions.question: A person who services household refrigerators wants Type I certification. Under 82.161(a)(1), who must offer the certification exam the person passes?

options.A: An approved technician certification program
options.B: Any school that teaches refrigeration, whether or not it is approved
options.C: The manufacturer of the person's recovery equipment
options.D: A state contractor licensing board

questions.explanation: Persons covered by 82.161(a)(1) "must pass a certification exam offered by an approved technician certification program," and no program may issue certificates unless it "has been granted approval by the Administrator."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

options.A: No, because Subpart F applies only to persons who maintain, service, or repair appliances
options.B: Only if the center also sells refrigerant
options.C: Yes, because Subpart F also applies to persons disposing of such appliances, including small appliances
options.D: Only if the units each hold more than five pounds of refrigerant

questions.explanation: Subpart F "also applies to persons disposing of such appliances (including small appliances and motor vehicle air conditioners)."

questions.question: A technician working on a dehumidifier needs to know which parts belong to its refrigerant circuit. How do the definitions describe a refrigerant circuit?

options.A: Only the compressor and its electrical controls
options.B: The parts of an appliance that are normally connected to each other (or are separated only by internal valves) and are designed to contain refrigerant
options.C: Every part of the appliance, including its cabinet and external wiring
options.D: Only the hoses and gauges a technician connects during service

questions.explanation: Refrigerant circuit means "the parts of an appliance that are normally connected to each other (or are separated only by internal valves) and are designed to contain refrigerant."

questions.question: A technician's recovery hoses have connectors designed to close automatically or to be closed manually when disconnected, minimizing the release of refrigerant. Which defined term describes these connectors?

options.A: Self-sealing valve
options.B: Process stub
options.C: System receiver
options.D: Low-loss fitting

questions.explanation: A low-loss fitting is a device that connects "hoses, appliances, or recovery and/or recycling machines" and "is designed to close automatically or to be closed manually when disconnected." A self-sealing valve is "a valve affixed to a container of refrigerant."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Low-loss fitting means any device that is intended to establish a connection between hoses, appliances, or recovery and/or recycling machines and that is designed to close automatically or to be closed manually when disconnected, minimizing the release of refrigerant from hoses, appliances, and recovery and/or recycling machines.

questions.question: A self-contained room air conditioner for residential air-conditioning uses R-441A. How does 82.154(a)(1) treat R-441A in this end-use?

options.A: It is exempt only when the unit holds less than five pounds
options.B: It is exempt only from the sales restriction
options.C: It is exempt from the venting prohibition and from the requirements of Subpart F
options.D: It is exempt only in household refrigerators and freezers

questions.explanation: The listed exempt end-uses for R-441A include "self-contained room air conditioners for residential and light commercial air-conditioning," and listed substitutes "are exempt from this prohibition and from the requirements of this subpart."

questions.question: A Type I technician stops working as a technician in 2026. Under 82.161(a)(4), how long must the technician keep a copy of the certificate?

options.A: Until three years after no longer operating as a technician
options.B: Until the wallet-sized card expires
options.C: One year after the last service job
options.D: Five years from the date of certification

questions.explanation: "Technicians must maintain a copy of their certificate until three years after no longer operating as a technician." While working, they "must keep a copy of their certificate at their place of business."

options.C: The hauler, who delivered it
options.D: Whoever last serviced the refrigerator
